name: Hindu nationalism
summary: Hindu nationalism, in its dominant form Hindutva, holds that India is the homeland and holy land of the Hindu nation, bound by common culture, history and (in Savarkar's account) blood. It seeks a polity expressing Hindu civilisational values, with a uniform civil code, protection of the cow, curbs on conversion and a strong, unified state. Its economic thought, Upadhyaya's Integral Humanism, rejects both capitalism and communism for a harmony-based third path stressing duty, swadeshi and the unity of spiritual and material life.
scope: The mainstream Hindutva current of the Sangh Parivar: Savarkar's Essentials of Hindutva (1923), Hedgewar's and Golwalkar's RSS, Upadhyaya's Integral Humanism (1965) as the Jana Sangh and BJP philosophy, and the BJP's 2024 manifesto. It excludes the older reformist Hindu revival movements and Nepalese Hindu monarchism except as background. Many economic, social and foreign-policy questions are not addressed by founding texts, so those answers are low confidence; where the BJP in office differs from the doctrine the answer is noted.

keyFigures.name: Deendayal Upadhyaya

sources.usedFor: The 2024 BJP programme: UCC, CAA, simultaneous elections, welfare, defence and economy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The BJP manifesto promises Ayushman Bharat cover up to Rs 5 lakh for poor families and seniors, a targeted state guarantee rather than a full universal system.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The manifesto only promises a periodic review of the national floor wage; Hindu nationalism has no doctrine of substantial wage rises.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Integral Humanism criticises capitalism and socialism alike, while the BJP in office leaned toward market growth, so adherents do not answer clearly either way.

public-ownership.rationale: Upadhyaya warned against excessive state power and economic centralisation, and the BJP has pursued privatisation, so broad public ownership is not an adherent position.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Nothing in the founding texts sets tax rates on the rich; the doctrine stresses harmony between classes over redistribution.

unions-good.rationale: The doctrine favours cooperation of workers and owners; the RSS-linked labour wing exists but unions are not a defining concern.

property-fundamental.rationale: Integral Humanism treats the economy as subordinate to dharma and society, so property is neither absolute nor rejected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The doctrine wants economic activity guided by dharma, but the party in office has favoured business-friendly policy, leaving no clear stance.

cut-welfare.rationale: The manifesto expands free rations, health cover and housing-type welfare for the poor, which runs against cutting welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects class-based socialism and offers no scheme of collective worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The party stresses border security and counter-terrorism; surveillance for that aim fits its security posture though no text states it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Social conservatism of the RSS family points against legal recreational drugs, though no text addresses drug policy directly.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Hindutva organisations have resisted limits on speech they see as defending Hindu interests, and critics note their own hostile rhetoric, so adherents oppose broad hate-speech laws.

strong-leader.rationale: The RSS model stresses disciplined hierarchy and one supreme leader (sarsanghchalak), and its supporters admire decisive leadership, though doctrine does not call for bypassing institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: Integral Humanism holds the state is a necessary organ of society under dharma, only warning against unlimited state power.

limit-guns.rationale: The manifesto has no gun policy; India already has strict gun laws and the issue is not part of Hindutva thought.

empower-police-military.rationale: The manifesto promises stronger border infrastructure and security, and the movement emphasises a strong, disciplined nation.

decide-locally.rationale: The party seeks one nation, one election and common rolls, and Hindutva stresses a single unified nation over devolution.

rehabilitation.rationale: No documented position on penal policy.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Socially conservative RSS-family morality is against legalising sex work, though no text addresses it.

traditional-family.rationale: The Sangh Parivar upholds the traditional Hindu family as the unit of society and opposes same-sex marriage.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The RSS supports decriminalisation but opposes same-sex marriage and same-sex adoption.

abortion-legal.rationale: Adherents are not reported as campaigning on abortion; India's law is permissive and no party doctrine addresses it.

more-religion-public.rationale: Hindu nationalism seeks a Hindu polity with cultural-religious symbols (Ram Mandir, Ramayan Utsav) in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Hindutva has no racial-justice agenda and Savarkar treated Hindu national unity as the goal; related caste reservations are debated within the movement.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Traditional family and complementary role views of the Sangh Parivar sit poorly with the claim that gender is mainly social.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Integral Humanism places the nation's cultural identity (Chiti) at the centre, and it is the core aim of Hindutva as national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Upadhyaya's organic view of society favours evolutionary change through national character, though the movement has also pushed abrupt reforms such as repealing Article 370.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The movement favours restricting entry of illegal migrants, and CAA fast-tracks only non-Muslim refugees, but it has no stated overall cut in immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Hindu nationalists stress national sovereignty and distrust outside bodies, but no text sets out a position on the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Upadhyaya's swadeshi-and-small-industry strand favours self-reliance, though the BJP in office has liberalised trade; adherents lean sceptical.

nation-first.rationale: Hindutva is a nationalism that puts the Hindu nation's interests and sovereignty first, as in the manifesto's Viksit Bharat aim.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No documented stance; India's foreign policy has traditionally opposed intervention but the doctrine says little.

open-borders.rationale: Savarkar defined the nation by a fixed fatherland and holy land with a common blood, and the movement backs border fencing.

limit-growth.rationale: The manifesto aims for the third-largest economy and a manufacturing hub, so growth is prized over limiting it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The manifesto has no clear commitment; party policy balances growth and green goals.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The manifesto stresses technology, manufacturing and indigenous satellites, though the doctrine itself is spiritual.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The BJP backs nuclear weapons and growth in energy capacity, though no text in the sources addresses nuclear power specifically.

revolution-justified.rationale: The RSS pledged loyalty to the Constitution to get its ban lifted in 1949 and works through organisation and elections.

experts-over-public.rationale: No documented position; Integral Humanism stresses an organic society without technocracy.

central-planning.rationale: Upadhyaya rejected both capitalism and socialism and warned of concentration of power in the state.

socialized-markets.rationale: Integral Humanism proposes a third path but without endorsing public or worker-owned market enterprises specifically.

land-value-tax.rationale: No documented position on land taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No documented position on inheritance tax.

basic-income.rationale: The manifesto prefers targeted welfare and job creation to unconditional cash payments.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The swadeshi and small-industry strand of Integral Humanism favours protecting domestic industry, as in Make in India.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The manifesto sets state targets for manufacturing hubs and strategic sectors, showing support for directed development.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Upadhyaya's economics favoured decentralised small industries and wide ownership over concentration in firms or the state.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects socialist abolition of private economic life and treats the economy as a legitimate part of life under dharma.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No Hindu nationalist text proposes it; the BJP government works through the Reserve Bank.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Integral Humanism's organic harmony of classes echoes corporatism, but no text proposes state-recognised wage-setting bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: The movement works within multiparty elections (Jana Sangh, BJP) and the RSS pledged loyalty to the Constitution, though critics note a single-party dominance aim.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hindu nationalism in India is republican, though in Nepal its supporters have campaigned for the monarchy and a Hindu state.

democracy-best.rationale: Integral Humanism accepts democracy as one ideal to be harmonised with others, and the movement contests elections.

direct-votes.rationale: The movement works through parties and representative institutions, with no push for direct legislation.

workers-councils.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects Marxist class politics and councils replacing parliament.

right-to-secede.rationale: Hindutva stresses an undivided India (Akhand Bharat) and Savarkar and Bhagwat both opposed separatism.

natural-rulers.rationale: Hindutva opposes hereditary caste hierarchy in principle, though critics claim it protects upper castes.

political-violence-never.rationale: Savarkar had links to revolutionary groups and the movement treats armed resistance as legitimate in some cases.

war-builds-character.rationale: The RSS prizes discipline and physical training but no source states that war builds character.

separate-church-state.rationale: The movement seeks a Hindu polity and rejects Western-style secularism as a European product, as Integral Humanism describes.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Integral Humanism treats dharma as principles of harmony, not religion, and Hindutva is defined as national culture rather than scripture law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defence and justice belong to the state under Integral Humanism, which warns only against excess.

military-superiority.rationale: The manifesto promises stronger defence and border security, and the movement favours a strong India.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Savarkar held Hindus are one nation chiefly through common blood alongside shared culture and land.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Integral Humanism says cooperation and harmony are central and conflict is a sign of degradation, rejecting class struggle as history's driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The doctrine seeks harmony among classes and not enforced equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The manifesto marks a Janjatiya (tribal) Year but no source gives a view on indigenous land authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Hindu nationalism stresses colonial-era cultural revival, though no source says it demands reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Hindutva stresses a shared civilisational homeland across the subcontinent, but a union of religiously similar nations is not stated.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects individualism and puts duty to dharma and the whole above self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Integral Humanism treats society as an organic whole with duty (dharma) as the governing principle, ahead of individual rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Integral Humanism sees life as an integrated whole, but nature's intrinsic worth is not spelled out.

limit-population.rationale: Some Sangh figures call for population control, but this is debated and not a firm doctrine.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Upadhyaya favoured small industry and swadeshi but did not call industrial civilisation a disaster.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The manifesto backs technology and manufacturing while the doctrine stresses preserving cultural continuity.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The manifesto favours digital governance tools but no source describes algorithmic decision-making.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: No documented position; the government has sought traceability from platforms.

restore-past-order.rationale: Hindu nationalism looks to civilisational revival but also claims modernity and growth, so adherents do not sharply prioritise restoration over progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Integral Humanism is itself a guiding philosophy and the movement sees policy as flowing from Bharatiya culture.

direct-action.rationale: The Sangh Parivar combines electoral politics with street mobilisation, but its main route to power has been elections.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Integral Humanism embraces material progress of body, mind and soul together.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Savarkar treats the varna division of functions as a social institution that may disappear when its purpose is served, not as something to abolish at once.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The doctrine rejects socialism's economics and speaks of dharma-guided distribution rather than strictly by need.

production-for-use.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects pure profit-seeking but does not endorse production for use alone.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects Marxist exploitation theory and class conflict in favour of harmony.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Integral Humanism criticises socialism and class-based politics and calls conflict a sign of degradation.

collective-farming.rationale: The doctrine rejects collectivism; Upadhyaya favoured decentralised small producers.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Integral Humanism criticises capitalism as exploitative but does not link it to imperial war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Integral Humanism accepts a legitimate state under dharma, and the party runs large tax-funded programmes.

harm-principle.rationale: The doctrine places community and dharma above individual liberty, so the state may restrict adults beyond harm prevention.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects the social-contract view and sees society as an organic entity with its own life.

conscription.rationale: The RSS prizes discipline but no source states a position on conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The doctrine centres on belonging to an organic national community, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Integral Humanism subordinates economy to dharma and the state to society, not the state as a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Integral Humanism wants the material needs of the person met alongside spiritual ones, but does not discuss liberty theory.

media-academia-power.rationale: Hindutva supporters complain of an entrenched left-liberal academy and media, though no founding text states it.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Savarkar stressed common blood for Hindus, but no source states a position on ability differences between races.

organic-representation.rationale: Upadhyaya's organic view of society fits representation through communities and bodies, though not spelled out.

total-state.rationale: Integral Humanism warns that unlimited state power harms dharma and leads to neglected duties.

national-rebirth.rationale: Hindu nationalism descends from nineteenth-century revival movements and speaks of national cultural renewal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Akhand Bharat is a cultural-civilisational ideal and the sources show no programme of expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Nothing in Hindutva or Integral Humanism proposes feudal oaths as the basis of authority.

bound-labor.rationale: Savarkar said varna is an institution made for society, which may disappear, and Hindutva opposes hereditary caste hierarchy.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: No documented position, though Hindutva critics of academia hold that scholarship carries bias.

universal-morality.rationale: Upadhyaya treats dharma as universal principles of harmony and law that bring peace and progress.

single-common-good.rationale: Integral Humanism holds that society has a unified soul (Chiti) and seeks harmony over a clash of interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The RSS later supported the formation of Israel and Hindutva writers favour it, though it is not a core position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The CAA gives a route to citizenship for persecuted minorities from neighbouring countries, though it is religion-selective.

revive-national-language.rationale: Savarkar called Sanskrit a sacred possession of the race and the movement promotes Hindi and Sanskrit, though not as a revival of a dead language.

school-vouchers.rationale: No documented position; the manifesto mentions new institutions only.

economic-freedom.rationale: Integral Humanism attacks both capitalist and socialist extremes, so it does not tie political freedom to economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Upadhyaya stressed morality in politics and honesty as a principle, but rule by example alone is not stated.

national-self-determination.rationale: Savarkar defined the Hindu nation by shared land and culture and sought independence for it.

force-without-un.rationale: The BJP stresses strong security and national sovereignty and has acted without outside approval, though no source states this.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Integral Humanism joins material and spiritual aims, with dharma as guide, and does not make reason the only guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Hindu nationalism distinguishes citizens from infiltrators, though no source gives a welfare rule.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The manifesto offers free rations and benefits without a work requirement and no source states otherwise.

class-collaboration.rationale: Integral Humanism holds cooperation and harmony are central and conflict is degradation, so classes are partners.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Culture grows from the national Chiti and is to be preserved, so inherited institutions should not be sacrificed.

dominated-front.rationale: The BJP follows a multi-aligned foreign policy; no source supports a front against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects an international class and puts workers within the nation and its culture.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The RSS excludes women from membership and upholds traditional roles, but the BJP backs women's reservation and equality in law.

ban-interest.rationale: No documented position and the BJP government uses ordinary banking.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Savarkar excluded caste hierarchy within Hindus and the movement does not propose race-segregation law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Integral Humanism sees the state as an organ of society under dharma, not a ruling-class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The manifesto's growth and manufacturing aims imply energy supply, but no source states fossil fuel policy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Golwalkar called on non-Hindus to adopt Hindu culture or accept subordinate status, and Savarkar's test is attachment to the land.

elite-replacement.rationale: Some Hindutva voices claim demographic conspiracies, but this is not a defining position.

proportional-representation.rationale: The manifesto seeks one election and one roll under the existing first-past-the-post system.

national-mission.rationale: Upadhyaya claimed Bharatiya culture's integral vision offers the world an alternative, but not spreading government form.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The RSS upholds traditional roles and critics rather than adherents describe patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The BJP campaigns on anti-corruption and against dynastic elites, as its manifesto's anti-graft pitch shows.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The movement stresses support for security forces, and no source supports accountability for past abuses.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Integral Humanism wants the state to guide economic and cultural life under dharma, not limited to defence and property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Savarkar's idea of common blood is not a ban on mixing, and Hindutva speaks of inter-caste unity.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Savarkar and Bhagwat reject caste hierarchy, but Golwalkar placed non-Hindus in a subordinate position, so adherents only partly agree.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects socialism so the question does not arise.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The RSS supported Israel, and Hindutva rejects colonial labels for Hindu-majority nations.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Jana Sangh from 1951 backed a uniform civil code and the BJP manifesto promises to bring one.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The Sangh Parivar campaigns against conversion from Hinduism and promotes reintegration of converts as people who share Indic culture.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: The Jana Sangh founded by Syama Prasad Mukherjee demanded a ban on cow slaughter.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Hindutva supports teaching Hindu cultural heritage, but sources document no explicit position on state religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects socialism so the withering-state question is not part of its thought.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Integral Humanism accepts democracy as an ideal to be harmonised, and the movement contests elections, though it grounds authority in dharma too.

trade-surplus.rationale: Swadeshi self-reliance strand favours export strength over import dependence, but no text states a trade-balance aim.

population-transfer.rationale: Golwalkar demanded non-Hindus accept subordinate status or assimilation, but mainstream Hindutva today does not call for expelling minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The RSS drills for strength and accepts defensive and collective force, so it rejects absolute non-aggression.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Integral Humanism says cooperation and harmony are central to Bharatiya culture and conflict is a sign of degradation.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The RSS itself was banned in 1948 and 1949 and the movement supports strong state action against separatists, though it resents bans on itself.

separated-powers.rationale: Upadhyaya warned that unlimited state power harms dharma, which fits checks, but no text sets out separation of powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects Marxist class politics and the vanguard idea.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The manifesto centres poor, youth, farmers and women as its four pillars of development with free ration and health cover.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: No documented position; India has little council housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: No documented position on strike law.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Some Sangh figures stress population growth as a burden, but it is not a stated doctrine.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Hindutva stresses one national culture and unity, though it also praises unity in diversity, so only a weak agreement.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: No Hindu nationalist source supports lotteries, and the movement works through elections.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The RSS was itself repressed in the 1975 Emergency, so adherents are cautious, while security hawks accept special powers.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The manifesto supports MSP and free rations but no source documents price caps.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Sangh Parivar has criticised state control of media in the Emergency era, though it favours cultural guidance of content.

party-commands-army.rationale: The RSS pledged loyalty to the Constitution and the movement works within the civilian-military framework.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The BJP backs a CAA fast track for selected groups, but generally supports strict citizenship rules.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The RSS-linked party model stresses organisational discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Hindu nationalism stresses national sovereignty, though no source mentions the EU.

head-commands-forces.rationale: No documented position on India's parliamentary system.

church-by-bishops.rationale: No documented position on episcopal church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Hindutva is defined by Savarkar as national culture rather than religion, and Hindutva groups do not claim priestly rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Integral Humanism makes the nation and its Chiti the foundation, rejecting the Marxist call for defeat of one's own government.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The article notes campaigns against academics and the removal of a Ramayana essay, showing support for restricting works that offend Hindu feeling.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The BJP follows a multi-alignment policy and the doctrine does not address alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Nothing in the doctrine supports banning rentals.

people-in-arms.rationale: The RSS stresses drill and discipline, but no source calls for replacing the professional army with a militia.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Swadeshi and village-industry themes in Upadhyaya's thought favour village life, but it is not stated as morally healthier.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Savarkar opposed Partition and Hindutva groups treat Akhand Bharat as an undivided civilisational homeland.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: No documented position, though Hindutva supporters criticise the English-educated elite.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Golwalkar criticised exclusive Abrahamic monotheism and Hindutva sees Bharatiya culture as distinctive, but many adherents also stress tolerance of other faiths.

death-penalty.rationale: The BJP government has kept the death penalty and the movement stresses tough security responses, though no source states it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sangh Parivar social conservatism has resisted sex education, though no source states it.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: No documented position, and Hindu nationalists have promoted claims from mythology as history rather than creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Social conservatism of the RSS family favours restriction, though no source states it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Savarkar tied Hindu identity to shared blood and land, but India's law mixes birth and descent and no source states a preference.

minority-language-support.rationale: Savarkar treats Hindi and Sanskrit as the national and sacred tongues, so state support for minority languages is not a priority.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Jana Sangh opposed special treatment for communities through its uniform civil code demand.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Integral Humanism puts community and culture first and does not celebrate nonconformity.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Integral Humanism wants a swadeshi economy alongside political independence, but does not require transformation of property.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The RSS accepted the Constitution after its ban, though early writings criticised it for not reflecting Manusmriti.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: No documented position and critics debate the BJP's record on freedoms.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: India under the BJP is both aid donor and a developing economy; no source gives a view.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The BJP conducted the 1998 tests and stresses self-reliant national defence.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Hindutva treats the land from the Indus to the seas as the holy fatherland and Akhand Bharat as the ideal, so ceding land is resisted.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Integral Humanism makes economic activity subordinate to dharma and the good of the whole society.

collective-defense.rationale: The BJP stresses strong defence ties, though India has avoided formal alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: No documented position, and the movement backs ending Kashmir's special status.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The movement wants state control of temples to end but not a general curb on religious institutions; Hindutva also seeks Hindu institutions free of state control.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: India's president is already ceremonial; no documented position.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Hindutva stresses an undivided India and opposes separatism firmly, with the state ready to maintain unity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The Jana Sangh demanded an end to Jammu and Kashmir's special status and the BJP later revoked Article 370.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Integral Humanism makes dharma the sovereign, with no sacred or divine ruler in modern Indian Hindu nationalism.

character-from-environment.rationale: Integral Humanism sees a person as integrated body, mind, intellect and soul but takes no stance on nature versus nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Dharma as law binds all in Upadhyaya's thought, even the state.

space-expansion.rationale: The manifesto backs the space programme but not as a central civilisational goal.

leader-cult.rationale: The RSS opposes personality worship in principle, but supporters honour their leaders; no firm doctrine.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects class struggle, so the claim sits outside its view.

land-redistribution.rationale: Members joined the Bhoodan voluntary land gift effort, but the movement does not back forced redistribution.

refugee-return.rationale: Hindutva stresses Hindu rights to return and shelter, e.g. the CAA, though no source speaks to a general principle.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Akhand Bharat is a cultural ideal and the sources show no claim to territory by nationality.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Savarkar defined Hindutva as national culture and not as religious doctrine, and Hindu nationalism has no tradition of punishing leaving a faith.

women-must-cover.rationale: No Hindu nationalist source supports compulsory covering of women.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Akhand Bharat is a civilisational homeland, not a union of linguistic kin peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Golwalkar wanted non-Hindus to merge into the national mainstream rather than hold separate institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The CAA offers refuge to persecuted groups, but no source states the doctrine on this.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Integral Humanism says spiritual and material progress must advance together and rejects the Marxist view of history.

ban-cartels.rationale: No documented position on competition law.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Hindutva-aligned supporters often criticise judicial overreach, but no text states the principle.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The manifesto backs women's reservation (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) but not equal parity in all public bodies.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The swadeshi theme favours self-reliance but not a closed bloc with colonies.

moral-incentives.rationale: Upadhyaya's stress on duty and dharma suggests moral motives but he does not reject material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The movement works through mass organisation and elections, not insurgent foco strategy.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Savarkar opposed hereditary caste hierarchy and said varna should disappear when it has served its end.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Hindutva campaigns revised textbooks centred on Hindu civilisation and the 'saffronising' of syllabi is documented.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Hindu nationalism arose against colonial claims of Western superiority, as in the Arya Samaj.

patriotic-education.rationale: The RSS shakhas teach loyalty to the nation, and Hindutva supports instilling national pride in schools.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preferences do not apply in India; the movement opposes caste reservation expansion in part, with mixed signals from Bhagwat.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Integral Humanism critiques capitalism but does not predict its collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Akhand Bharat and cultural influence across the subcontinent is a Hindutva theme, though not stated as a foreign policy aim.

delink-world-market.rationale: The manifesto seeks integration and exports for India while stressing self-reliance.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects Marxist theory generally, with no view stated on this claim.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Hindutva stresses social unity and the state promoting harmony, though caste discrimination is its own debate.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The RSS accepted the Constitution but critics note it once opposed it, so no documented position.

elective-rulers.rationale: The movement contests elections for office and accepts democracy as an ideal in Integral Humanism.

minority-veto.rationale: Integral Humanism sees the nation as an organic whole with a collective soul, not a compact needing every member's consent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Dharma binds rulers in Indian tradition, but no source gives a theory of lawful resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The BJP works through parliament and holds parliamentary sovereignty, though no source states the doctrine.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Cow protection and Hindu ethical traditions give animals moral weight, as the Jana Sangh's cow-slaughter ban demand shows.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The movement bans cattle slaughter but accepts other animal use, with no stated rule for research.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Integral Humanism says each part of society owes duty to the whole under dharma, which includes help for the weak.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The RSS mobilises members for national service and political work.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Integral Humanism does not use a ruling-class framework.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Swadeshi themes imply caution about foreign dominance, but no theory of extraction is stated.

native-born-offices.rationale: Hindutva's idea of loyalty to the land and the movement's stance on Sonia Gandhi's foreign birth point toward it, though not a formal doctrine.

party-own-road.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects communism, so the question does not arise.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The swadeshi theme in Upadhyaya's economics stresses national self-reliance, echoed in the manifesto's manufacturing goals.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Akhand Bharat and the demand for undoing Partition support it, though no concrete claim is stated.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The manifesto marks tribal welfare but no source states a position.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Savarkar and Golwalkar expressed sympathy for Axis policies, and Hindutva supporters are wary of anti-fascist framing.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Integral Humanism condemns communism and hardly condemns fascism, so adherents often accept condemning communism but the equivalence is not stated.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American question with no Hindu nationalist position.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Hindutva campaigns to remove or replace monuments linked to Muslim rulers, but also wants its own heroes preserved.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Integral Humanism says Western ideals did not suit India and Bharatiya culture needs its own integral approach to state and economy.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The RSS accepted civilian rule under the Constitution, and the Indian army does not play a political role.

office-by-exam.rationale: The manifesto promises transparent recruitment and a law on paper leaks, but nothing about doctrine.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Swadeshi themes favour protecting strategic industries, but the BJP has welcomed foreign investment.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Integral Humanism has no delegate model and the movement works through ordinary representation.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The BJP governs through parliament and the budget process, though no source states the principle.

single-official-language.rationale: Savarkar treated Hindi as the national tongue and the movement promotes it, though the BJP also accepts other languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Swadeshi themes suggest caution, but no documented position.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Hindutva supporters tend to reject framing of unequal outcomes as discrimination, but nothing is stated.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Integral Humanism says material progress alone is not the aim and that body, mind and soul must advance together.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: No source supports it and India has officially opposed cross-border insurgency.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The Sangh Parivar has long attacked foreign-funded conversion NGOs, and the government has restricted foreign funding, though no source states the principle.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Some Sangh voices urge population control rather than incentives for more births.

residents-only-property.rationale: Hindutva backed ending Kashmir's special status that had such rules, though no stated principle.

job-guarantee.rationale: The manifesto offers jobs through growth, not a guarantee; MGNREGA is a rival party scheme.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Dharma as law and duty is central to Integral Humanism.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Golwalkar's writings treat minorities with intense suspicion, but the question is a conspiracy claim that mainstream adherents do not state.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Sangh Parivar upholds marriage and the traditional family.

local-production.rationale: Swadeshi and small-industry themes favour local production, though the manifesto aims for a global manufacturing hub.

informal-organisation.rationale: The RSS is a hierarchical and disciplined organisation with uniformed drill.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Hindu nationalism stresses sovereignty, though no source states it.

religious-nation.rationale: Savarkar insisted Hindutva is not religion but nation, though the movement fuses culture with Hindu religion in practice.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: India's government stresses strategic autonomy and sovereign equality.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The manifesto's one-nation approach favours central coordination.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Integral Humanism recognises personal property as part of life while rejecting collectivism, but without stating this form.

defeat-communism.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects communism and the Sangh Parivar has long opposed it.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The manifesto uses public and private channels such as ONDC and Ayushman Bharat with private hospitals.

religion-illusion.rationale: Integral Humanism makes spiritual aims central to a full life and treats dharma as basic.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Integral Humanism criticises capitalism, while the BJP embraces growth, so no clear line.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects economic-determinism, though no source discusses women's equality there.

socialized-care.rationale: The Sangh Parivar upholds the family as the place of care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Savarkar championed Sanskrit-based language reform, but no source shows mainstream adherents demanding a purge.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Upadhyaya favoured decentralised small units but not cooperative communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: The movement ended Kashmir's special status but settling majority groups in minority regions is not an adherent position.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Integral Humanism is Upadhyaya's explicit third way, rejecting both capitalism and communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Hindutva grounds claims such as the Ayodhya Ram temple on a historical and religious tie to land, and Savarkar's holy land concept.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Sangh figures expressed admiration for Hitler but mainstream Hindu nationalism does not deny the Holocaust.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The RSS has supported decriminalisation though opposes same-sex marriage.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The RSS was banned in 1948 and during the Emergency and the movement contests elections, so it rejects suppressing opposition in principle.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Hindutva groups have protested insults to Hindu deities, but doctrine does not state a blasphemy law.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Hindu nationalism arose against colonial rule and resists colonial economic exploitation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine outside Integral Humanism, whose view of Dharma excludes it.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Hindutva is defined as national culture rather than religion and does not authorise removing rulers by religious law.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Hindutva rejects identity-based class framings and promotes Hindu unity.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: India's law recognises transgender people, and the RSS has taken a cautious stance, so no clear line.

assisted-dying.rationale: Social conservatism leans against it, though no source states a position.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Integral Humanism presents itself as a third way beyond capitalism and socialism, combining the best of each.

alienated-labor.rationale: Integral Humanism's critique of capitalism is about exploitation, not alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Golwalkar demanded assimilation, but the RSS today says Muslims are descendants of Hindus and can join, so adherents differ and Western countries are outside scope.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Integral Humanism places dharma over the state, but dharma is defined as law and not as God's will.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Hindutva groups have defended Hindu dress while supporting hijab restrictions in some schools, so no consistent view.

social-market-economy.rationale: Integral Humanism wants a market economy harmonised with social duty, and the BJP combines markets with welfare.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The manifesto promises stronger border infrastructure and defence, and the movement prizes a strong nation.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: India's strategic autonomy policy under the BJP favours keeping out of blocs, but no source states it.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The BJP campaigns against dynastic politics.

property-franchise.rationale: Nothing in Hindu nationalism supports limiting the vote by property.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is not a documented position.

reification.rationale: Integral Humanism critiques capitalism but not through reification theory.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The doctrine does not use this class critique.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Dharma as law that brings harmony is central, but no text on legal procedure.

racial-franchise.rationale: Hindutva defines the nation by culture and land and its parties contest elections open to all citizens.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The Sangh Parivar campaigns against interfaith marriage seen as conversion, and several BJP states have passed laws on it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Some Hindutva groups call for boycotts, but the leadership does not officially endorse them.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Hindu nationalism draws on reform movements like Arya Samaj, while others defend tradition.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Integral Humanism warns that capitalism with democracy enables exploitation by a small group holding real power.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Social conservatism leans against it, though no source states it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Integral Humanism says spiritual aims are central to human life and Hindu nationalism is a religious-cultural movement.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The manifesto promises stronger security and the movement is pro-order.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The RSS is known for relief work, but the BJP also runs large state welfare programmes.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The RSS excludes women from membership, though some Hindu traditions have women teachers, so adherents lean against.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Sangh Parivar upholds the family but the BJP backs women's equal rights in law.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Hindu nationalism ties belonging to the land, and the movement opposes giving foreigners political rights.

abolish-ip.rationale: No documented position, though the manifesto promotes domestic manufacturing and innovation.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The RSS runs uniformed shakhas with drill and discipline to train young members for national service.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The BJP is committed to India's own nuclear weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Strategic autonomy favours no foreign bases, though no source states it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Integral Humanism criticises exploitation by capital and values productive work.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The RSS drills for defence and the movement accepts force in defence of the nation.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Savarkar presents Hindu identity as a continuous nation from the Vedic Aryans to the present, sharing blood, culture and holy land.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Conservative views of gender lean against it, though no source states it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Hindu nationalism honours Savarkar and revolutionaries as patriots, and the movement celebrates those who died for the nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Integral Humanism joins spiritual and material, but not as a struggle of good versus evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Savarkar's holy land concept makes India the cultural centre for Hindus, though diaspora relation is not stated.

culture-before-state.rationale: The RSS was founded for cultural social work before entering politics, and Integral Humanism stresses culture as the nation's soul.

god-not-male.rationale: Hinduism includes goddess worship, but no source states a political position.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: No source supports it, and the RSS excludes women from membership.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Swadeshi favours Indian ownership, but no source states majority group control.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects socialism so the test is not its own.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The manifesto supports public provision of basic services in part, but no source gives a rule.

second-chamber.rationale: India has the Rajya Sabha and the BJP works within it.

municipal-property.rationale: Integral Humanism favours neither collective nor private-only ownership by communes.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The manifesto and Hindutva favour a strongly unified national state.

family-wage.rationale: The Sangh Parivar upholds the male-breadwinner family, though no source states a wage law.

person-over-state.rationale: Upadhyaya describes the individual as an integrated being of body, mind, intellect and soul, and state power as limited by dharma.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Integral Humanism says humans have body, mind, intellect and soul and that spiritual aims like Moksha cannot be pursued in isolation from material progress.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The Jana Sangh demanded an end to Jammu and Kashmir's special status, treating regional autonomy as revocable by the national centre.

gm-crops.rationale: The Sangh's swadeshi wing has opposed GM crops while the government offers mixed policy.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Hindutva organises Hindus as a national community, not a race, though Savarkar uses blood terms.

racial-pride.rationale: Savarkar treats Hindu ancestry and racial unity as grounds for pride, but it is not framed as a racial category of the modern kind.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: India's formal doctrine is defensive but Hindutva writers favour strength, so no clear line.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Savarkar defines the nation by common land, blood, culture and holy land, treating Hindus of all languages as one nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Hindu nationalism opposes separate religious treatment, as shown by the Jana Sangh's uniform civil code demand.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Hindutva groups speak of separatism and external forces, and Bhagwat condemned separatism, though a plot is not formally stated.

future-generations.rationale: Integral Humanism stresses continuity of the national community across generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: No documented position, though the movement stresses women's roles in family.

arms-reduction.rationale: The movement favours military strength and the BJP expands defence.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The RSS drills in uniform but not armed, and the BJP supports the state's security monopoly.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The RSS disciplines members for national defence and rejects refusal of war orders.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Integral Humanism favours labour-capital cooperation without a stated bargaining model.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Swadeshi themes and the Global South rhetoric of the BJP lean this way, though no source states it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects revolutionary class politics and accepts the state under dharma.

sacred-nation.rationale: Savarkar's definition makes India both fatherland and holy land and the nation a continuing community of shared blood and culture.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The movement stresses national unity across regions rather than internal exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Integral Humanism treats the person as an integrated being with a common soul and dharma as universal law of harmony.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Hindu thought as presented by Vivekananda sees Advaita Vedanta as core, and Hindu leaders stress that all paths lead to one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: The manifesto promises raising MSP and a farm infrastructure mission to shield farmers.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The BJP tested weapons in 1998 and stresses a national deterrent.

ban-fgm.rationale: FGM is practised by a small Muslim community, and no Hindu nationalist source documents a position.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The BJP supports equal inheritance rights under the Hindu succession reform, but no source states it.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Savarkar treated Hindi and Hindusthani as the living national tongue regardless of regional names.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The movement does not promote chiefs in lawmaking, though it marks a tribal year.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Savarkar treated Hindi and Sanskrit as national tongues, so adherents expect integration, but no source states a requirement.

voter-id.rationale: The BJP backs common electoral rolls and has supported tighter voter identification.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Jana Sangh pressed uniform laws but also state recognition of Hindu norms, so no clear stance.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Integral Humanism says democracy must be reconciled with other ideals and is not only a procedure.

premarital-sex.rationale: Social conservatism leans against it, though no source states it.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The BJP governments have used shutdowns in Kashmir and elsewhere, though no source states it as a principle.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The manifesto uses in-kind and targeted schemes rather than this tax.

women-suffrage.rationale: The BJP backs women's reservation in legislatures and Hindu nationalism does not oppose women's vote.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Integral Humanism makes dharma central and Hindu nationalists defend their faith.

race-social-construct.rationale: Savarkar spoke of common blood as basis of nationhood, so adherents do not take race as mere construct.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The manifesto includes women's programmes but no source states agencies.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Hindu nationalism stresses sovereignty and India has not joined the ICC.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Hindu traditions have no single inerrant scripture and Savarkar treated Hindutva as national culture.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Integral Humanism rejects planned socialism, so no defence.

national-church-status.rationale: Hindu nationalism seeks a Hindu polity where Hindu culture holds a special place.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The Jana Sangh demanded ending Kashmir's special status and Hindutva opposes group autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Hindutva opposes the plebiscite idea for Kashmir and treats it as part of India.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Hindutva calls Partition a wrong, which is a colonial-era border, and favours undivided India.

simple-living.rationale: Integral Humanism limits material goals as only one part of life, though simplicity is not stated.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Savarkar defines a Hindu through a land that is both fatherland and holy land, tying nation to the spiritual homeland.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: No Hindu nationalist source supports this, though some state governments have defended police encounters.

close-ties-china.rationale: The border disputes and security stress of the manifesto imply caution about China.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The CAA offers refuge for persecuted religious minorities of neighbouring countries and the movement stresses protecting Hindus abroad.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The manifesto targets welfare at the poor through free ration, health cover and electricity schemes.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The movement is organised through the RSS, a party and affiliates and does not reject parties.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The BJP campaigns against corruption, though no source states this.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Hindutva organises politics on Hindu identity, so it rejects denominational limits.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Integral Humanism joins material progress to Bharatiya cultural values and presents it as India's way of modernity.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The BJP argues a uniform civil code gives women equal rights, including in divorce.

national-resource-control.rationale: The swadeshi theme stresses national control of the economy and its resources.

filial-duty.rationale: The Sangh Parivar upholds the traditional family and duty to parents as part of Hindu social values.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Traditional family and complementary role views of the Sangh Parivar sit poorly with this critique of fixed categories.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Hindutva favours a single national community and criticised separate treatment of communities, so executive power-sharing by community does not fit.

self-ownership.rationale: Integral Humanism treats the person as embedded in society and dharma, but no source takes a stance on self-ownership.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from Integral Humanism, which rejects pure capitalism for a duty-based harmony; the question of process versus outcome is not addressed.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed by founding texts or the BJP manifesto; adherents have no settled view.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not addressed directly; Hindutva texts argue about communal and caste divisions rather than racism as such.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from Integral Humanism's view that dharma stands above the state and from Savarkar's moral account of the nation.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from Integral Humanism's swadeshi emphasis on employment and the unity of spiritual and material life.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from the civilisational view of India as a distinct culture and the Hindutva preference for independent power centres.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from Integral Humanism's rejection of both capitalism and Marxism, including Marxist economics.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from Integral Humanism's mix of national devotion and service to the whole community, including labour.

material-over-identity.rationale: Savarkar and Upadhyaya put cultural and civilisational identity at the centre and reject a purely materialist politics.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from Integral Humanism's rejection of communism; one-party socialism is not discussed.

missingStatements.text: Citizenship rules should give a fast track to persecuted members of particular religions from neighbouring countries.
missingStatements.rationale: The BJP manifesto promises to implement the Citizenship Amendment Act and the party's record makes religion a criterion for citizenship.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow single-country citizenship rule; the audit answers religious-nation neutrally and the issue is not a dividing line across many ideologies.

missingStatements.text: A person belongs fully to the nation only if they regard its land as both their fatherland and their holy land.
missingStatements.rationale: Savarkar's central definition of a Hindu is one who regards the land from the Indus to the seas as fatherland and holy land.

notes: Golwalkar's early writings demand non-Hindus adopt Hindu culture or accept subordinate status, while current RSS statements treat Muslims and Christians as descendants of Hindus who may join; answers follow the mainstream today. The BJP in office has been more market-friendly than Integral Humanism suggests.
